title: Subtoken latency continuum and KV reverb model
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Add fine-grained observable signals and a lightweight model that attributes per-subtoken latency and cost to runtime components and KV cache behavior.

Background: Current request-level and coarse token buckets miss transient reverb effects caused by KV prefetches, cross-request cache pollution, and conditional kernel selection for long sequences. Teams need a low-overhead way to answer: which subtokens and which stages (prefetch, kernel, serialization, network) actually moved the needle for latency and cost on production traffic?

This ticket will: (1) instrument a chronology stamp at the subtoken emission boundary, (2) emit compact event spans that tag cache-affecting operations (KV lookup, prefetch triggered, cache-evict), (3) synthesize a per-subtoken attribution vector that approximates upstream cost share, and (4) add dashboard/alerting surfaces for regressions.

Telemetry schema (compact):
- emit_type: "subtoken_span"
- request_id, span_id, parent_span_id (opaque strings)
- model_variant, hardware_tier, route
- sequence_pos (subtoken index), token_text_hash
- wall_ns (emission time delta), cpu_ns, gpu_ns_estimate
- kv_event: one of [hit, miss, prefetch, evict, none]
- kv_latency_ns (if applicable)
- kernel_path: short tag (e.g., attn_v2, fused_mm)
- batch_size_at_emit
- sample_flag: small integer (0=full, 1=sampled)

Design notes and trade-offs:
- We prefer small, flat spans to avoid heavy protobuf payloads. Payload budget per request capped at ~1KB when sampling, and 30bytes per-subtoken when running non-sampled lightweight mode.
- Two data paths: sampled (full spans + kv latency) and sketched (histogram buckets per-subtoken plus a compact kv bitset). Sampling configured by route and SLA tier.
- Estimating GPU_ns: infer from kernel selection and micro-benchmarks rather than trying to fetch wallclock from GPU for each emission to avoid contention.
- Cache attribution model: assign direct KV latency to subtokens that requested the key; assign amortized prefetch cost to subsequent subtokens in window W=8 by default, with decay curve parameter alpha. This captures reverb without overcharging early subtokens.

Implementation plan:
1) Runtime hook: add emission_hook() that records sequence_pos, chosen kernel tag, batch size, and emits a tiny event to the local ring buffer. (ENG code touches runtime/emit_hook.cc)
2) KV layer tagging: augment KV client to annotate prefetch and miss events with request_id and key_hash. Expose a compact descriptor to emission_hook via threadlocal metadata.
3) Local aggregator: process ring buffer periodically (every 50ms) to coalesce events into records suitable for the telemetry pipeline. Two serializers: JSON-line for sampled traces, and thrift-lite for sketched streams.
4) Telemetry ingestion: update samplers in ingestion pipeline to decode the new span type and attach to request traces. Add a transform that computes per-subtoken cost attribution and appends attribution fields to the aggregated trace.
5) Dashboards and alerts: add a latency heatmap by sequence_pos, stacked by kv_event and kernel_path; create an alert when average KV-amortized latency for sequence_pos <-> pos+8 increases >15% week-over-week.

Acceptance criteria:
- Emitted spans show up in tracing for 100% of sampled requests and for 0.1% of unsampled requests without causing CPU overhead >3% p95 on tail-heavy traffic.
- Aggregation job computes per-subtoken attribution and stores results in observability store (metrics bucket) for queries by model_variant and route.
- Dashboards display latency heatmaps and a new "KV reverb" metric; alerts fire in test scenario with synthetic prefetch storms.

Rollout plan:
- Canary: enable for internal dev org and for 5% of production traffic on non-critical routes. Monitor CPU/ingestion costs for 72 hours.
- Ramp: 25% then 100% for sampling pipelines; maintain 0.1% lightweight sketching across all routes by default.

Migration and backward compatibility:
- Telemetry worker will accept both old and new span types. Backfill not required; new attribution is forward-looking.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should prefetch amortization window be adaptive to model context length? (proposal: keep tunable; default W=8)
- Do we need HSM-level signing for trace envelopes on private deployments? (security review flagged)
